full_judgment:
2. Opposite party Chowdhury Syndicate Limited is a private limited Company engaged in construction work on contract under the Government. A tender was called for construction of a 200 foot long bailey bridge over Chandankhali River within Chittagong division. Being the lowest, the tender of the opposite party was accepted on 16-7-91 and the company was given the work order under Memo No. 2651/R dated 10-8-91 of the Superintending Engineer, Roads and Highways, Chittagong, to complete the work within one year and three months. The contractor started constructing the Bailey bridge, which was all but complete. Suddenly the bridge fell into the river and the contractor had to incur an extra cost for restoring the bridge and rejoining the same and submitted his bill claiming the extra cost and refund of the amount deducted on account of VAT. There was a dispute over the contractor's claim for payment of the extra cost and refund of the amount deducted on account of VAT. The Chief Engineer, R&H, appointed Mr. JB Barua, Superintending Engineer, R&H (Planning), Dhaka, as the arbitrator. The Arbitrator commenced arbitration proceedings, recorded evidence of the parties and found that the contractor was not liable for falling of the 200-foot long bailey bridge in the river, which was an accident, and that he recovered all parts of the bailey bridge at his own cost and rejoined the same and was entitled to payment of the bill for the extra work. The arbitrator further found that there was no condition in the contract/tender for deduction of vat from the contractor's bill and so directed for refund of the amount deducted on account of VAT. But payment having been refused by the Additional Chief Engineer as per award of the arbitrator, the contractor filed the miscellaneous case (Case No. 23 of 1996) before the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong, for making the award Rule of court. 

 8. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmood, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party (contractor), has relied on the decision in the case of Government of Bangladesh vslalaluddin Ahmed 37 DLR (AD) 27. In this case the plaintiff- respondent made a reference to the arbitrator, who made the award in favour of the defendant appellant for payment of money. The plaintiff-respondent instituted the suit on the ground, amongst others, that the award is illegal, void and without jurisdiction, have been passed beyond four months of the reference in violation of the condition of Article 3 of the first schedule to the Arbitration Act. No objection was raised by either of the parties to the arbitration proceedings that the award could not be passed as the period of four months had already expired. The Appellate Division approvingly considered the decisions in the cases of Seth Shambhu Nath vs SM Surja Devi, AIR 1961 Allahabad 180 and Ganesli Chandra Misra vs Artatrana Misra, AIR 1965 Orissa 17 where it was held that where after expiry of four months, the parties submitted themselves to the jurisdiction of the arbitrators and took part in the proceeding, the arbitrators did not act without jurisdiction in passing the award. Their Lordships of the Appellate Division did not accept the views of the High Court Division that the award was void ab initio on the ground that it was beyond the statutory period of limitation (four months) and allowed the appeal. In this connection we may refer to the decision in the case of Federation of Pakistan vs H Ghulam Mohiuddin, PLD 1960 (WP) Lahore 677. In this case the bid of the respondent-contractor for supply of soap to North Western Railway was accepted. Clause 11 of the Contract between the parties provided for reference to arbitration in case of a dispute. The arbitrator was to be nominated by the General Manager, North Western Railway. The dispute having arisen, the Chief Engineer was nominated arbitrator by the General Manager. The Chief Engineer was later promoted to the rank of General Manager, but continued the arbitration without any objection by the respondent and finally gave his award. In this case it was held by the Single Bench that the respondent is estopped by his conduct from challenging the arbitrator's jurisdiction to act as such. It is patent that the petitioners (Government and others) submitted themselves to the arbitration and participated in the arbitration proceedings from the beginning to the end without any objection and so they are estopped from challenging the jurisdiction of the arbitrator at this stage and, more so, when they practically submitted no objection against the award in their formal written objection filed before the learned Subordinate Judge under section 30 of the Arbitration Act. So, it cannot be said that the arbitrator acted without jurisdiction in passing the award.
